name: Sony Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones
description: Sony over-ear wireless headphones with active noise cancelling, designed for commuting, travel, and all-day listening. They combine a lightweight headband, cushioned ear cups, Bluetooth multipoint connectivity, and app-based EQ/ANC controls. USB-C charging and long battery life support extended use, with optional wired listening when needed. The understated light-gray finish targets users who want comfortable isolation and consumer-friendly sound without bulky gamer styling.

reviews.content: Comfortable for long flights. ANC knocks down engine drone well. Light gray looks less fingerprinty than black.
Sound is V-shaped fun — great for pop. Not neutral studio monitors, and that's fine for commuting.
Clamping force loosened after a week to the sweet spot. First day was tight on my glasses.
Mic for calls is average outdoors. Office calls are clear enough. Don't expect headset-grade voice.
Battery easily survives a workweek of mixed use. USB-C charging is quick. Fold flat in a backpack.
App has useful EQ and ANC levels. Multipoint to laptop/phone is reliable after the latest firmware.
Ear pads got warm in summer walks. Breathable enough for trains, sweaty for summer runs — use buds then.
Build feels solid for the price tier. Hinges don't creak. Sony branding understated on the headband.
Transparency mode helps hear announcements. A bit artificial but safer than blasting ANC forever.
Bass can bloom on default EQ; dial it back for podcasts. Voices become clearer immediately.
Paired instantly with iPhone and Android. No drama. LDAC available on my Pixel for hi-res listening.
Headband padding is soft; after 3 hours I still forget I'm wearing them. Rare for over-ears.
Case not included on my bundle — annoying. Bought a third-party sleeve. Headphones themselves: excellent.
ANC isn't flagship XM5 territory, but for the money it's very effective on buses and offices.
Right cup controls took a day to learn. Once mapped in my muscle memory, great walking UX.
Slight plastic creak if I fold carelessly. Treat the hinge kindly. Sound remains the reason to buy.
Gaming on PC has noticeable latency via BT. Fine for single-player; competitive needs a dongle/wired.
Colorway is office-friendly. Don't look like RGB gamer cans. Wear them to meetings without stares.
Wind noise on calls near the bike path is bad. Pause music and use phone for important calls.
Leakage at high volume is modest. Library use at moderate levels didn't bother neighbors.
Firmware update fixed a random disconnect quirk. Keep Headphones Connect updated.
Compared to older Sony WH models, this feels lighter and less fatiguing. Happy upgrade.
Pads are replaceable — good longevity plan. Stock pads still plush after months.
Auto-pause when removing works most times. False triggers when I adjust glasses occasionally.
Neutral fans may prefer other brands; fun listeners will smile. Know your preference.
Travel pillow + these = long-haul survival kit. ANC naps are real.
Bluetooth range drops through two walls. Normal for the class. Stay in-room for stable audio.
Spoke to support about a defective ear cup LED; quick swap. Service experience was positive.
Wired mode works when battery dies — underrated safety net on long trips.
Soundstage is in-head, not speaker-like. Immersive modes try; I keep them off.
Matte finish hides scuffs from backpack zippers better than glossy cans I've owned.
Spouse and I argue over who gets them for flights. Solving by buying a second pair.
Touch panel registered rain droplets as taps once. Wipe before play in storms.
Voice assistant double-tap is optional — disabled mine to avoid accidents.
Weight distribution is excellent. No hotspot on the crown of my head.
Not the last word in isolation; glasses arms leak a bit of noise. Still a daily driver.
EQ preset 'bright' fixed muffled voices in Netflix dialogue for me.
Packaging was minimal; headphones were pristine. No odor from pads.
Latency watching mobile YouTube is acceptable. Lip-sync rarely bothers me.
Cheap knockoffs don't match Sony's ANC algorithm tuning. Paying for the brand made sense here.
One side played quieter until I cleaned the mesh. Maintenance tip: soft brush monthly.
Works as a Zoom mic in a pinch; dedicated mic still clearer. Hybrid WFH stack.
Folded size fits a work tote easily. Commute companion of the year for me.
Drops in a cafe once — scuffed, still perfect sonically. Survivable build.
Default ANC is strong; adaptive modes are fine. I leave it on max for planes.
Treble can get sharp on poorly mastered tracks. EQ shelving helps. Source quality matters.
Battery percentage in OS is rough; app meter is better. Still lasts longer than my patience for charging.
Gifted a pair — recipient texted 'why did I wait'. Strong gift item for remote workers.
Slight hiss with ANC in silent rooms if you're sensitive. I only notice before music starts.
Bottom line: comfortable, capable wireless ANC headphones with fun tuning and strong battery for everyday and travel use.
